title: The graph removal lemma for every fixed graph
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the graph removal lemma of Erdős, Frankl and Rödl for an arbitrary fixed finite graph H on k vertices: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0, depending only on H and ε, such that every finite graph on n vertices with fewer than δ nᵏ labelled copies of H can be made H-free by deleting fewer than ε n² edges; equivalently (far form), a graph from which at least ε n² edges must be deleted to destroy all copies of H has at least δ nᵏ labelled copies. Also included is the counting lemma used in the proof: if parts s x (one for each vertex x of H) are robustly dense with density at least d along the edges of H, with 2kη ≤ dᵏ and #(s x) ≥ 4k/dᵏ, then at least (dᵏ/4)ᵏ ∏ #(s x) injective maps send H into G with f x ∈ s x. Mathlib has the regularity lemma and the triangle removal lemma, but not the removal lemma for a general H.
